label: H.R. 4018

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini. (rated before the current eligibility rules; kept)

summary: H.R. 4018 directs federal agencies to speed up the process for issuing permits, licenses, and leases related to exploring and recovering critical minerals and resources from the ocean floor. The bill establishes deadlines for federal departments to create seabed mapping plans, identify critical minerals essential for defense and energy, engage with international allies on mineral development, and submit reports to Congress regarding private sector interest and international benefit-sharing mechanisms.

affected_groups.effect: Benefit from streamlined, predictable, and expedited processes for obtaining federal permits, licenses, and leases for offshore seabed exploration and commercial mineral recovery.
Required to complete numerous specific actions, mapping plans, mineral identifications, international engagements, and congressional reports within a 60-day deadline.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies (Department of Commerce, Department of the Interior, Department of State, Department of Defense, Depart

affected_groups.effect: Engaged by U.S. officials to collaborate on scientific research, commercial development, and exploration within their jurisdictions.

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of Commerce, through NOAA and in consultation with the Secretaries of State and Interior, to expedite review and issuance of exploration licenses and commercial recovery permits under the Deep Seabed Hard Mineral Resources Act within 60 days.
Requires the Secretary of the Interior to establish an expedited process for reviewing and approving prospecting permits and leases under the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act within 60 days.
Mandates the creation of a seabed mapping plan for priority areas of the U.S. outer Continental Shelf within 60 days.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior, in coordination with the Secretaries of Defense and Energy, to identify critical minerals derived from seabed resources that are essential for defense, infrastructure, manufacturing, and energy within 60 days.

Requires the Secretary of Commerce, coordinating with other secretaries, to engage with key international partners and allies to support seabed mineral exploration, extraction, processing, and environmental monitoring within 60 days.
Mandates two specific reports to congressional committees within 60 days regarding private sector mining interest and the feasibility of an international benefit-sharing mechanism.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or budget appropriations to carry out the expedited permitting, mapping, and reporting requirements.

Any alterations to environmental protection thresholds or specific legal standards under the underlying acts, other than a general instruction to ensure efficiency and competitiveness without compromising environmental and transparency standards.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 4018 directs federal agencies to speed up the process for issuing permits, licenses, and leases related to exploring and recovering critical minerals and resources from the ocean floor. The bill establishes deadlines for federal departments to create seabed mapping plans, identify critical minerals essential for defense and energy, engage with international allies on mineral development, and submit reports to Congress regarding private sector interest and international benefit-sharing mechanisms.
summary_detail.significance: The bill aims to reshape U.S. policy regarding domestic deep-sea and outer continental shelf mining to secure critical mineral supply chains independent of foreign adversaries. Because the legislation focuses on accelerating administrative procedures and interagency coordination rather than altering existing underlying environmental laws or appropriating specific project funds, its practical impact depends on how executive agencies execute the mandated 60-day reviews and planning processes.

title: To unleash America's offshore critical minerals and resources.
